newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Law would bloc any Schindler buy of Thyssen unit.
newsitem.headline: Law would bloc any Schindler buy of Thyssen unit.

text.p: Leading world escalator and elevator maker Schindler Holding AG said anti-cartel laws would be a major barrier to any potential acquisition of the elevator business of Germany engineering group Thyssen AG.

Asked whether Schindler would be interested in the Thyssen unit if it were to come on the market, Schindler chairman Alfred Schindler also told a news conference that prices were very high for those kinds of business at the moment.
Schindler said one question would be whether a high purchase price would detract from the company's interest in pursuing internal growth.
"In principle there is no reason not to pursue it (if the Thyssen's business came on the market) but in many cases we would simply not be permitted to by cartel law," Schindler said.
"Cartel laws, especially in the United States, are very tough," he added.
Schindler said there was only limited room for accomodating anti-cartel authorities with spin-offs or other portfolio adjustments.
Schindler said the price for any such acquisition would be another major factor.
"The price for medium to large companies is generally at least equivalent to annual sales," he said, adding:
"Then you would also be in direct competition with your internal growth."

Schindler said earlier in the news conference that the group needed to grow to keep up with a competitive world market, but would concentrate on internal growth because only a few independent companies remained to be bought after over a decade of consolidation in the industry.
Finally, Schindler said other factors to consider would be whether an acquisition was located in a country with higher or lower growth and whether its product line was complementary.
Schindler was replying to a question about what would happen if Thyssen decided to spin off its elevator business as part of a cooperation with Krupp.
